claims.claim: Severian was Bishop of Gabala in Syria.
Severian flourished in the fourth and fifth centuries and died after 408.
Severian was a popular preacher in Constantinople from around 400 until 404.
Severian became the enemy of John Chrysostom and helped condemn him at the Synod of the Oak.
Severian came to Constantinople around 400 and became a favourite of the Empress Eudoxia.
When John Chrysostom went to Asia in 401, he entrusted Severian with the pastoral care of the Church of Constantinople.
Fragments of Severian's commentary on the Epistles of St. Paul have been preserved.
The Fragmenta in epistulam ad Philippenses survives in catenas (chain commentaries).
Severian was described by Gennadius as 'in Divinis Scripturis eruditus, et in Homiliis declamator admirabilis' (learned in the Divine Scriptures and an admirable declaimer in homilies).
